lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Right, everyone. Porridge or eggs, and how did we all sleep? Hands up for both questions.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Both, Joan. Eggs and porridge, and I slept like a man who'd earned it.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: You snored from about two until four, Dale. I know because I was awake for most of it.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Then you got a free concert, mate. Most people pay for that.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Porridge. Quick. The first trunk's waiting and it won't fell itself.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Eggs, please, if that's okay. I slept, mostly. Sorry, the wind kept me up a bit.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Lunch report, everyone. Two sandwiches, an apple, and a biscuit Biscuit doesn't know about.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: That dog knows, love. That dog always knows. He can smell a crust through a tin.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Sorry, should I hide mine too? I don't want to be the one he follows home.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Eat faster, all of you. Twelve minutes and we're back on the lane.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: The break's twenty minutes on the sheet, Marta. I checked. We've got eight more.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Eight. Fine. I'll spend them sharpening.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Quiz night, my loves. First question: how many trees did this crew fell today? Marta, you're not allowed to answer.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Loads, Joan. A great big load of them. Do I get a point?

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: He doesn't. And I know the real number, so you'd better have it right, Joan.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: I'd have to check the yard tally, so I'll pass. I don't guess on quiz nights.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: That's why nobody lets you play, love. Fine. Next question. Who left the kettle empty?

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Decks are filling and the fire's slow. We stack tight tonight or we lose half a morning tomorrow.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Tight's my middle name, mate. Well, it's Albert. But tight's close.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: If the short lengths go on the top deck, the long ones fit underneath. I measured both.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Do it Priya's way. She's right, and I want us all in before dark.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Can we be quick? Sorry. It's just that the light's going.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: We're quick, love. Ten more minutes and I'll walk you in myself.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Paid, paid, paid! Everyone hear that? That's the sound of a man who can afford snacks.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: We heard, sunshine. Half the island heard. Biscuit's already waiting by the locker.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Good. That one's earned. Tomorrow we start earning the next.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: I'm putting mine aside for Ana's course. Sorry, that's boring. But I'm really happy.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: That's not boring, mate. That's the best use of money on this whole island.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Rain's coming from the west, steady, not gusting. The low lanes will be soft by midday.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Then we cut high this morning and come down once it drains.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: I'll keep the truck on the ridge track, then. The low one turns to soup in this.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Soft lanes, wet bark, slippery logs. Lovely. I'll be carrying them like bars of soap.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Everyone take dry socks off the rack before you go. I'm not nursing anyone's feet tonight.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Ground rules, for anyone new or anyone who's forgotten. One feller per lane. Shout before it goes. The cradle isn't a bench.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: And the food in the blue tin is mine. That's a rule too, mate. Unofficially.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: It isn't, love. The blue tin's for everyone. I'm the cook, so I make the rules about tins.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: And check the lean before you notch, not after. That's the one people learn the hard way.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: And supper's at dusk, everyone helps clear up, and nobody touches my arcade score.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Does anyone remember my first day? I racked my axe upside down. Sorry. I still think about it.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Mate, my first day I put my boots on the wrong feet. Walked half a mile like that. We all start somewhere.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: You racked it upside down once and never again. That's all anyone needs from a new hand.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Hear that, sunshine? That's practically a medal from Marta.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: That empty bunk's bothering me, and I don't bother easy. Whoever the company sends next, I hope they play cards.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: As long as they don't cook. One bad cook per crew, and that job's taken.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: I hope they can fell. We're a pair of hands short, and the count shows it.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: I keep expecting them to walk back in. Sorry. I know they won't.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: People leave contracts early all the time, Tomas. They had their reasons. It doesn't have to mean anything more.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: You can see the shore from the middle ridge now. When we landed it was solid canopy.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: More than half gone. The second half always feels slower. It isn't. Keep going.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Less shade for lunch, mates. Nobody ever thinks about the lunch shade.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Odd, isn't it. Like a pub after closing. Too much room, and all the chairs up on the tables.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: I don't love how far you can see now. Or how far anything could see us. Sorry. Ignore me.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Look at that. Stumps all the way down to the dock. We did that, mates. Mostly me.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Mostly the axes. Then me. Then you, Dale, hauling it all off. Fair's fair.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: I'd want the numbers before I crowned anyone. But the stumps do look good from up here.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Everyone to the north lanes today. Fell the lot, haul it tomorrow. Faster that way.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: If we fell everything first, the yard sits empty today and overflows tomorrow. I'd split the crew.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Split it, then. Two fell, the rest haul. But I'm on the axe.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Mate, if you fell it all today, I'm carrying it all tomorrow. My back would like a vote.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Your back's had a vote every day this month, Dale. It always votes for lunch.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Why not ask the boss, love? That's what they're paid for. Allegedly.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: The boss has enough on. We sort our own lanes. Always have.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Somebody told me there was something by the dock. Has anyone else heard that? Sorry. I just want to know.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Somebody's been reading forums, love. Who told you? I'll have a quiet word.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: I don't want to get anyone in trouble. Sorry. Forget it. It was probably nothing.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: By the dock? That's water slapping the pilings, mate. Sounds like footsteps at night. Every dock does it.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Who said it, and when? If they can give me a time and where they stood, I'll write it down. If not, it's a story.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Here's a good one. Apparently someone saw a light in the trees past the burn pit. A light. In the trees. Fireflies, mates.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Sun off the water, or a lantern someone forgot. Don't start the night on a story.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Don't laugh at that one, Dale. Just get inside before the light goes.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Did they say what colour, and how high? Fireflies don't hold still at head height.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Can we not, Dale? Please. Not right before dark.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Leave it, sunshine. Tomas is right. If there's telling to do, it waits for daylight.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: I'll say it so nobody whispers it. I've been told someone heard a voice in the trees. I'm not saying I believe it.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Told by whom? A rumour passed through two people loses the useful parts first.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: That's my point exactly, love. By the time it reached me it had grown a beard.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: A voice? Somebody's radio carrying over the water. Or Tomas talking in his sleep again.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Right, cards. Joan and me against Priya and Tomas. Winners do the dishes. No, losers. Losers do the dishes.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Losers do the dishes, love, and you've had your hands in that sink most nights this month.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: I'll play, but I'm keeping track of which cards are gone. That isn't cheating. It's attention.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Okay, but I'm bad at this. Sorry in advance, Priya.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: You're not bad, Tomas. You fold too early. Hold on one round longer.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: New name at the top of the arcade board, my loves. Want to guess whose it is?

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: If it's not mine, the machine's broken. I'll have a look at it after supper.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Sorry. It's mine. I couldn't sleep. Is that okay?

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Okay? Sunshine, it's the best news all week. I'm going to frame it.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Whoever it is had energy left over after the day's cut. I'll find them more work.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Biscuit's carrying a glove. I think it's yours, Dale. There's jam on the thumb.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: That's not jam, that's strategy, mate. He'll trade it back for a crust.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: That dog eats better than half this crew. Mostly off Dale's plate.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Get it off him before it's chewed. Gloves aren't free. Neither's jam.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Count starts now. I want twenty trunks at the cradle by dusk, and I want the stumps clean.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Twenty trunks. That's twenty times I carry your ambition, Marta.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Twenty is doable if the yard keeps up. That's the part that usually gives first.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: I can run the truck between the lanes and the yard, if that helps. I'm faster in it than on foot.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Company's late with the pay. I'm telling the boss so tomorrow. Plainly.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Go on, love. I'll not say much myself. I'm busy adding up what I've got put by.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: I've got a stomach to feed, mate. The company can't pay a stomach in promises.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Take dates with you. When we were last paid, how many days are owed. The boss will take numbers better than temper.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Nobody's going out in that. Kettle's on. Who wants to hear about the night the bar cellar flooded?

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Me. Every time. Do the bit with the barrel and the man in the bow tie.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Me too, please. Talking helps with the noise of the wind.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: The gusts are coming every forty seconds or so. I checked the window frames. They're holding.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Everyone hold on. The mud's deep past the second bend. I'll take it in first, nice and slow.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Captain Tomas, mates. Best seat on the island, and the snacks ride free.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Look at him, all confident behind the wheel. Where's this lad at dusk?

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Still here. The truck just makes sense to me. Dusk doesn't.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Slow's fine. Stuck isn't. You know the difference better than I do.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Is everyone here? Sorry. I just like counting us before we go in.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: I count every evening too. Keep walking. I'll do it again at the gate.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Count us twice if it helps, sunshine. I'll count you.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: I counted at the last fence post. Everyone who left the lanes with us is walking with us.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Wind's swung round to the north since lunch. The leans we marked this morning won't all hold.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Then we re-mark them. Ten minutes now saves a trunk across the lane later.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Should I move the truck back from the edge? Sorry. I'd rather not have a tree on it.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Wind's on my side, then. Every tree that falls toward the track is a shorter carry.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Everyone in by dusk from now on. No stragglers, no last trunk. I'm not discussing why.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: If Marta's saying it, I'm listening. I don't need the why, love.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Agreed. And we walk in pairs. If you'd tell me what you saw later, Marta, I'd write it down.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Marta's never once called a day early. Not in all the years I've known her. Fine. In by dusk.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Thank you. Sorry. I'm just glad someone else said it first.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: Anyone else's boots still wet from yesterday? Mine squelch when I think about them.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: Stuff them with newspaper. Oh, wait. No newspaper. Stuff them with somebody's spare socks.

lines.speaker: trait:sociable
lines.text: Line them up by the stove, all of them. We'll make a little boot parade.

lines.speaker: trait:observant
lines.text: The fire pile's burning faster on the windward side. We should feed the other end.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: I'll take the other end. Somebody pass me the short lengths.

lines.speaker: trait:hard_working
lines.text: Feed both ends and it'll burn twice as fast. The cradle needs the room.

lines.speaker: trait:timid
lines.text: Are we nearly done? It's getting dim under the trees.

lines.speaker: trait:level_headed
lines.text: Last carry. Then we walk in together, at a sensible pace.

lines.speaker: trait:hard_working
lines.text: One more trunk would finish the lane. But I'll leave it for the morning.

lines.speaker: trait:skeptical
lines.text: A voice nobody can name, heard by somebody nobody can name. That's not news, that's weather.

lines.speaker: trait:sociable
lines.text: Who's got a story? Not a scary one. A daft one.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: I once lost a whole truck in a car park. Found it three hours later. Wrong car park.

lines.speaker: trait:reliable_driver
lines.text: Daft story: a goat once refused to get off a delivery ramp. I waited it out. Took an hour.
